extracted.intended_audience: internet journalists, editors, and readers interested in internet-native reporting and news selection
extracted.subtask_description: A journalist's selection framework for what counts as 'news' on the internet, prioritizing cultural-significance and pattern-detection over traditional hard-news criteria. Useful for reporters deciding which online phenomena to investigate and elevate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform behavior changes
rubrics_metrics.description: **Platform behavior changes** that affect how meaning circulates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about mechanics or policy/feature shifts on platforms that change distribution, visibility, or interpretation of content — i.e., changes that alter how meaning circulates online and therefore merit reporting as newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subculture eruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: **Subculture eruptions** — niche communities producing widely felt artifacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should prioritize moments when niche or subcultural activity creates artifacts (memes, trends, content) that bleed into broader culture or have outsized cultural impact beyond their original community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: **Format shifts** — new content forms (TikTok genres, Discord patterns)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on the emergence of new content formats, genres, or interaction patterns (e.g., new TikTok genres, Discord behaviors) that change how people create and consume media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic vector tracking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize tracing the origin and propagation paths of memes/ideas (who started it, how it spread) to explain cultural dynamics rather than treating virality as isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online-to-offline events
rubrics_metrics.description: **Online-to-offline events** — when posts cause real-world action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories are newsworthy when online speech or activity produces measurable offline consequences (events, protests, business impacts, legal outcomes). Emphasize causality from online content to real-world outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influencer drama with structural significance
rubrics_metrics.description: **Influencer drama** with structural significance (not just gossip)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between gossip and drama that reveal or affect underlying platform, economic, or cultural structures — only the latter merits reporting as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broderick test — new pattern vs old instance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this a new pattern or just an instance of an old one?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this question to filter stories: prioritize signals that indicate emergent patterns over isolated occurrences to avoid covering noise as if it were systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broderick test — explanatory value
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this tell us something about the platform / algorithm / culture?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the item provides insight into platform mechanics, algorithmic effects, or cultural dynamics; prefer stories that illuminate underlying systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broderick test — eventual mainstream relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Will the people not online care eventually?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecast broader relevance: prioritize stories that are likely to matter beyond niche online audiences and that may cross into mainstream concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broderick test — missed-by-traditional-news
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this a story we missed because it didn't look like 'news'?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a corrective: elevate phenomena that traditional newsrooms overlook due to format/venue, especially when they reveal important cultural shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demoted categories / deprioritized story types
rubrics_metrics.description: Demoted Categories: One-off viral tweets without context; "Brand X did Y" PR events; Established creator beefs without new dynamics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating isolated viral posts, routine corporate PR moves, or repetitive creator disputes as news unless they meet the criteria above (show new patterns, structural significance, or broader impact). These are listed as low-priority/anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevated categories / high-priority beats
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevated Categories: Telegram / Discord / private-platform reporting; Right-wing internet ecology shifts; AI slop / generative content reshaping platforms; Algorithmic injustice case studies; Subculture moral panics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that probes private-platform dynamics, political/ideological ecosystem changes online, generative AI's structural effects, algorithmic harms, and moral panics within subcultures — these are explicitly highlighted as beats with outsized significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern-oriented definition of news
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework expands the definition of news to "patterns of cultural production that mainstream news systems are too slow to catch."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a pattern-focused mindset: the goal is to surface recurring cultural-production dynamics rather than only discrete 'hard-news' incidents. This reframes newsworthiness toward cultural and platform patterns.
